patterns.name: Explicit norms and enforcement
patterns.problem: Participants may not know acceptable behaviour, while enforcement may be discretionary or difficult to contest.

components.name: Show relevant rules at the point of participation
Make enforcement criteria, responsibility, and procedure public
Provide reporting, sanctions, and review mechanisms

patterns.mechanism: visible rules → more comprehensible expectations → changed selection or conduct of participants

patterns.name: Structured retrospectives / debriefs with follow-up
patterns.problem: Teams repeat errors or lose learning because experience is not compared with goals, explanations, and subsequent action.

components.name: Assign responsibility and later verify implementation

patterns.mechanism: shared reconstruction → identify discrepancies → revise strategy → changed subsequent practice
patterns.assessment: core structured debrief is provisionally corroborated from convergent synthesis-level evidence, but the key S03/S04 support remains abstract-level in the live corpus pending full-text methods audit and deduplication; the full follow-up package remains documented

patterns.name: Explicit distribution of care work
patterns.problem: Listening, onboarding, relational maintenance, and distress management can concentrate on people who receive less recognition or have less ability to refuse.

components.name: Identify care work and who performs it
Assign responsibility and make workload negotiable
Recognise time, compensation, or workload offsets

patterns.mechanism: visible care work → negotiable allocation → less reliance on implicit availability → more equitable load
patterns.assessment: documented; direct causal evidence for redistribution remains scarce

patterns.name: Informal power and mandates
patterns.problem: People may control agenda, information, or decisions without authority that is explicit, bounded, or contestable.

components.name: Describe domain and limits of a mandate
Distribute access to skills and information

patterns.mechanism: identifiable authority → contestable expectations and limits → possibility of correction or revocation
patterns.assessment: the problem is documented more broadly than the proposed remedies

patterns.name: Consensus / consent / lazy consensus
patterns.problem: Groups need to authorise common action without excluding relevant objections or requiring simultaneous participation in every decision.
patterns.mechanism: different protocols structure coordination and objection costs differently; no single shared mechanism is assumed
patterns.assessment: protocols are well documented; comparative evidence on superiority is insufficient

patterns.name: Asynchronous decision-making
patterns.problem: Meeting-bound decisions exclude people unavailable in the same time window or require responses before they can process relevant information.

components.name: Escalation to another mode when needed

patterns.mechanism: no requirement for co-presence → contribution at different times → potentially broader access
patterns.assessment: context-limited; inclusive benefit versus synchronous decision-making remains uncertain

patterns.name: Conflict and dissent
patterns.problem: Contrary information may be suppressed, while relational hostility and persistent role conflict can harm work and retention.

components.name: Collect objections and alternatives before decision
Use a distinct process for relational conflict
Make division of labour and responsibility contestable

patterns.mechanism: contrary information → reassessment of assumptions → broader alternatives
patterns.assessment: the general claim that more conflict improves decisions is not sustainable; intervention types must be separated
